title: External quantitative ledger
reading_rule: Every value below was reported under its own publication's benchmark. No value is comparable to a MOTAR number. Class A matched external comparisons remain zero.

entries.environment: OmniDrones simulation; 0.9-radius, 1.2-height arena with 4-5 cylindrical obstacles (units not stated in source)
entries.target_type: scripted potential-field evader (speed 1.3 vs pursuer max 1.0); virtual evader in real trials
entries.sensor: PRIVILEGED relative state + binary line-of-sight mask; no camera or depth anywhere in the paper
entries.allowed_interpretation: The widely quoted '100% capture rate' is this: simulation only, in the Random and Passage scenarios, which the paper designates unseen/OOD. Wall is 0.987, not 1.000. Capture means the evader came within a capture radius of 0.3 before an 800-step cap. Three cooperating pursuers share ground-truth relative position through an LOS mask. No real-world capture rate is published.
entries.note_title_change: The v1 title differs from the current v4 title; the code repository still shows the v1 title.
entries.forbidden_interpretation: Do not subtract this value from any MOTAR rate, express it as a MOTAR advantage or deficit, or use it to rank this work against MOTAR.

entries.environment: OmniDrones; 6 m x 6 m x 3 m enclosed arena
entries.target_type: learned self-play opponent
entries.sensor: state-based observation with FOV frustum and cylinder-occlusion masking
entries.allowed_interpretation: The paper's primary metric is in-FOV rate, not capture. It defines no capture criterion and no capture radius, so this value cannot be read as a capture rate. The prose calls a 0.88 figure a 'capture rate' while the table labels that column In-FOV Rate; that inconsistency is unresolved in the source. The conclusion also states experiments were restricted to obstacle-free 1v1 engagements.
entries.forbidden_interpretation: Do not subtract this value from any MOTAR rate, express it as a MOTAR advantage or deficit, or use it to rank this work against MOTAR.

entries.environment: 3D stochastic Dubins simulation; NO static obstacles
entries.target_type: adversarial pursuer agents
entries.sensor: full relative state; no sensor model
entries.trials_or_episodes: no episode count; 50,000 s of simulated time
entries.allowed_interpretation: A collision here is an agent-agent event in an obstacle-free domain, counted as a safety metric. The paper defines no capture or success metric, has no static obstacles, and has no hardware results. Its Sec. 4.5 prose states '99% fewer collisions' for the fast-pursuer case while Table 3 shows 5.140 -> 4.666, about 9%; the tabulated values are the defensible ones.
entries.forbidden_interpretation: Do not subtract this value from any MOTAR rate, express it as a MOTAR advantage or deficit, or use it to rank this work against MOTAR.

entries.metric: tracking rate r_t (fraction of time within 3 m in x-y)
entries.environment: simulation, 20 m x 20 m x 3 m with 140 randomly deployed obstacles
entries.target_type: cooperative oracle; the target's ground-truth future trajectory is fed to the planner
entries.speed_condition: keys are the target's average speed in m/s (max 2.3 / 2.9 / 3.9)
entries.allowed_interpretation: A proximity-maintenance metric: the fraction of time the tracker stays within 3 m of the target in the x-y plane. It is not a capture or close-approach success rate, and the target's future path is given to the planner as an oracle.
entries.forbidden_interpretation: Do not subtract this value from any MOTAR rate, express it as a MOTAR advantage or deficit, or use it to rank this work against MOTAR.
